check_all.field_solver_note: native kisi: formula impedances only; the Node CLI kisi.mjs adds the 2D field solver
check_all.models: Impedance by formula (Hammerstad-Jensen, Wheeler, Wadell, IPC-2141); differential and coplanar lines can be off by 5–15 %. Losses: Wheeler/Huray/Djordjevic-Sarkar. Lanes run from device pin to device pin through series parts (estimated parasitics); side stubs of the lane nets are open stubs (unused pads, parts not fitted with their pad capacitance, the other path of a fork). Pads: a track inside an SMD pad has the pad's width; the rest of a part's pad is a capacitance from the pad's cross-section (with what lies below it), else an estimate per package. Eye: PRBS7, linear transmitter/receiver from the profile (a termination next to the receiver acts as its termination), without equalisation, jitter and noise; the step response with a DC point and checks (band edge, response before arrival, settling, passivity) in its warnings. Pairs are 4-ports (both lines on their own paths, coupled where they run together): loss and return loss Sdd21/Sdd11, the eye driven differentially, mode_conversion_db (worst Scd21 up to 1.5 × Nyquist) as information. Multi-drop lines along one path: the eye at every receiver (receivers), the worst counts. One N-port Touchstone file behind a connector with a port map (connector_ends.<connector>.touchstone.ports): the connector's other lanes in it are worst-case aggressors (crosstalk_peak; they enter at the connector without their board traces – an estimate). Shunt parts on the lane's nets (capacitors to ground, …) are in the channel at their pads. Lanes from connector to connector: board share only (loss, return loss, skew, TDR), no eye. Lanes ending at a connector: board share – loss, return loss and skew judged; the eye with the connector end model (kisi.json connector_ends.<connector>, default the profile's receiver or transmitter at the connector) – information (eye_board_share), or judged when a channel behind the connector (rest_loss_db or a Touchstone file) is given.

interfaces.notes: Lanes follow nets through series resistors (≤ 100 Ω), AC-coupling capacitors (≥ 1 nF) and small inductors; parts not fitted (DNP in KiCad or not in the chosen assembly variant) connect nothing, their pads stay as stubs. kind: ic-ic (eye checked), connector-connector (board share only, no eye), ic-connector (board share: loss, return loss, skew judged; the eye with the connector end model – connector_ends.<connector> in kisi.json, default the profile's receiver or transmitter; information unless a channel behind the connector is given), multi-drop along one path (the first two ends are transmitter and receiver at the ends of the path, the other devices receivers on side stubs: the eye at every receiver, the worst counts), open lines and multi-drop trees through series parts (not checked). Direction is a guess (termination next to the receiver), parasitics of passives are estimates from data/components.json. mpns (when present): the devices' manufacturer part numbers where the Value field does not show one.

gaps.issue: No regulator chain (field PI_REG): no power budget, no regulator load check.
gaps.where_to_find: Regulator datasheets: topology (buck/LDO/…), efficiency at the expected load, rated output current; input and output rails from the schematic.

gaps.issue: 4 supply rail(s) without a known voltage (found by their name, a pin name such as VBUS, VSYS, VBAT, VDD, or a field): kisi needs the voltage to put their loads and sources into the power tree, the budget and the IR drop. Found by name: confirm that each one is a supply.

gaps.where_to_find: Schematic: the regulator, load switch or connector that feeds the rail and its output voltage (regulator datasheet / voltage setting, USB VBUS 5 V, battery nominal voltage). A rail behind a ferrite, a 0 Ω link or a shunt takes the voltage of the rail before it.

source.note: VSYS follows VBUS while USB is present

write.note: Write the voltage where the rail appears in PI_REG: as the output of the part that feeds it (`+5V > VSYS@5V buck 90%`) or as a supply input (`VBAT@3.7V input`). Behind a ferrite, 0 Ω link or shunt use a pass element (`+3V3 > IMU_VDD pass r=0.5`: the voltage carries over; items[].write suggests it when kisi finds such a part). Net names with spaces in double quotes (`"/Power/VDD CORE"@0.9V`). Without a power tree: PI_SOURCE `NAME=<V>V` on the source part. Nets that are not supplies: ignore.
write.to: fields[] – the rail with its voltage as NAME@<V>V in a PI_REG entry

gaps.how: Fill the gaps in <board>.kisi.json next to the board (format: see `kisi config-template`), every value with a source; then run `kisi config-check <board>` and `kisi gaps <board>` again. Gaps marked 'not kisi.json' are fixes in KiCad.

channel.why: no buses or lanes between devices

impedance.why: no net with a target impedance (net classes such as 50Z or 90Z_Diff, or net_classes in kisi.json)
